_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The Lord does not see as we see; the Lord looks on the heart.
Open our eyes; we want to see.
Once we were blind, and we washed, and now we see.
The Lord is our light; whom shall we fear?
Wake, O sleeper, and rise; let Christ shine on you.
Once we were darkness; now we are light in the Lord.
The Shepherd leads us home; come, let us worship.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Imagine a lifetime of darkness, only voices and heat and the feel of the road, and then mud, and water, and light pouring in.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
This is what God does: passes over the tall and the likely, takes the youngest in from the sheep, and pours the oil on his head.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
For the Lord looks past the face we show the world and reads the heart we hide, and calls us anyway.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Wake, sleeper; rise from where you have lain; the light of Christ is already on your face.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
The Shepherd walks us through the valley to a table spread in the open. Come, let us worship.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Give us light. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The Lord looks not on the face but on the heart.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
We washed in the pool, and the light came flooding in.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Wake, O sleeper; Christ will shine on you.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
The Shepherd leads us home. Come, let us worship.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Amen.
